title: An inbound email claims a milestone shipped that's still open
author: off-by-one
description: The hundredth real recipe, and the fourth to read gmail (after email-claims-unfixed-issue, email-dangling-reference, and email-claims-unmerged-pr). Extracts every 'milestone #N' claim phrase (the shared seam_engine.milestone_claims grammar twelve sibling recipes already import) from an inbound email's own body and cross-checks it against the live milestone tracker's own state -- the identical milestone-claim check linear-comment-claims-open-milestone already runs against a Linear issue comment, applied here to the Gmail surface email-claims-unfixed-issue already opened. A milestone that exists but is still open is the seam: an email already sitting in a connected inbox disagrees with GitHub's own record, and nothing on either platform ever compares them. This closes the one leg the claims-open-milestone family (eleven surfaces: commit, issue-body, issue-comment, linear-comment, mention, milestone, readme, release, review-comment, slack-message, tweet) had never grown since gmail became a live toolkit in this engine (task 1046, email-claims-unfixed-issue). Fixture-only, MOCK ONLY, never a live network call -- the-hand gateway's connected Google account carries gmail.readonly among its granted OAuth scopes, but exposes zero Gmail-capable tools on the live gateway today, same WIP note email-claims-unfixed-issue already carries. Neither scope is new (ListMilestones sat on the oath table from founding; ListEmails has sat on the Gmail row since ROADMAP.md #16) and gmail+github is not a new toolkit pair (email-claims-unfixed-issue already proposed it).
confidence_notes: Age-gated by hours since the email's own received_at, holding linear-comment-claims-open-milestone's/email-claims-unmerged-pr's identical 0.85/0.5 bar exactly -- not an independently re-reasoned number just because the toolkit is new. A claim checked within 24 hours of the email landing might still be a race (the milestone actually closing out moments after the email went out) rather than a settled overclaim (0.5, below the 0.70 confidence bar, shown as a weighed-and-dropped coincidence, not hidden). At or past 24 hours with the named milestone still open, it is unambiguous (flat 0.85). The check itself is objective, same reasoning as every claims-open-milestone sibling: the claimed milestone's own live state field, verified against ListMilestones, not a guess about which tracker the sender meant. A named milestone that does not exist at all is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- a broken reference is email-dangling-reference's own seam, not this one's. A named milestone that IS closed is excluded too -- the claim was simply true. An email with no 'milestone #N' claim phrase at all produces no candidate. No text in this recipe's own headline/detail strings ever names or grades the sender -- CONTRIBUTING.md's 'No grading, ever' law, same as every recipe in this engine.
